title: Links, images and lists
brief:
Some tags need extra information, called attributes: a link needs to know where it goes, an image needs to know which file to show and what it shows.

Add three things to the page: a link to the university website that opens in a new tab, alt text on the image, and a list of three meeting rules. The checklist shows what is still missing.

vocabulary.gloss: extra information inside an opening tag, like href="…" or alt="…"
the address a link goes to
words that describe an image, read aloud by screen readers and shown if the image fails to load
an unordered (bullet) list, and one item in it

starterHtml:
Robotics Club

We are part of the University of Bedfordshire.

Meeting rules

Be on time. Share the tools. Ask questions.
starterCss:
body { font-family: Arial, sans-serif; padding: 1rem; }
img { border: 1px solid #ccc; }

checks.label: There is a link (a) whose href starts with https://
The link opens in a new tab (target="_blank")
The image has alt text that is not empty
There is a bullet list (ul) with at least three items (li)

hints: A link looks like the university website. Put it inside the first paragraph.
To open in a new tab, add a second attribute: target="_blank". Attributes are separated by a space.

Replace the rules paragraph with
  • Be on time.
  • Share the tools.
  • Ask questions.
. And put words inside the empty alt="" — say what the picture shows.
